answers.answer: Cursor-using Discord friends who ship personal projects but struggle to make them valuable to people outside the group; they build what interests them rather than what others might value. Excluded: vibecoders whose primary goal is self-amusement through absurd, shocking, or novelty-first builds where outward value is not the point.

Situation: Discord friends post personal projects to the group showcase. Trigger: after repeatedly shipping and posting varied projects (throwing stuff against the wall), none gain meaningful traction or clicks. Fact: observed pattern of low or no engagement across multiple showcase posts. Inference: they accept not every project will appeal widely but expected at least some to stick.

Go from scattered try-post-and-hope showcase cycles to seeing a clear direction: understand what they enjoy building from past attempts, what others respond to, and focus on the overlap where their strengths match something others actually value.

Audience: Discord group peers in the showcase. Desired impression: seen as encouraging builders toward small successes — helping each other turn a hobby into something functional and valued, not just self-amusement; mutual respect, kindness, and social glue in the group.

Want to feel accepted and part of the group when putting work out — normal encouragement (a pat on the back) after trying. Avoid feeling like they do not fit in when showcase posts get no feedback at all.

Buying: compare and adopt dev tools (especially Cursor) while token costs rise and rate limits tighten — stay value-conscious on spend vs capability. Co-creating: peer-teach newcomers how Cursor and the interface work; group tries to be helpful, but showcase feedback and reviews are weak. Transferring: walk away or pivot from projects before they should — not because the build is bad, but because they could not communicate outward value in terms others care about (inference from observed abandon-after-no-traction pattern).

Extreme: lack of marketing skills — group can program, vibe-code, and create but cannot articulate or position outward value; observed main bottleneck to showcase traction and differentiation from other vibe-coding communities. (User labeled severity severe/extreme.)

Gains for Cursor Discord friends who ship personal projects: (unexpected/delight) self-doubt turns into felt competence; (expected) emojis, likes, and chat interactions on showcase posts; (desired extension) recognition that carries beyond the showcase into the Discord general chat; (unexpected/delight) recognition by community leaders / ambassadors.

Usual: start another project (throw-more-at-the-wall). Sometimes: abandon Cursor and chase more expensive models (Anthropic, Codex) hoping the model leap closes the gap. Big temptation: evolve into fancy UIs and colorful pictures with unexplained mechanics behind a polished presentation — novelty/chrome instead of outward value.

Strongest observed signal is absence: after weak or no showcase traction, they quit interacting with the group (go quiet) rather than iterating on outward value. Source: owner observation of Discord showcase/group behavior. Strength: moderate — pattern of non-interaction is visible; motives inferred.

Priority sequence (not named earlier as a job): (1) Autonomy — AI as a safe space to create independently — most important; (2) Competence — nearly equal, usually follows autonomy (doubt → felt skill); (3) Only then consider others' needs — family, close friends, Discord peers — including the tension of isolation from friends while buried in AI work vs creating value for close friends in the group. Values' outward north-star work sits at step 3; it lands after autonomy and competence are felt.

Priority job (elevated): Autonomy — safe space to create freely with AI (also named creativity, liberty, freedom). Why highest: huge attraction of AI work and vibe coding; traditional developers are autonomy-starved so it is valuable there too; listed as a human need under names like autonomy/creativity/liberty/freedom. Competence is nearly equal and usually follows. Only after autonomy and competence are felt do they turn to others' needs and creating value for close Discord friends.
answers.conflict_note: User elevated autonomy as higher priority with broader evidence (vibe-coding attraction, autonomy-starved developers, Maslow-adjacent needs).

answers.answer: Pass — profile is a usable basis for solution design. Segment, priority (autonomy→competence→close-group value), pains, gains, alternatives, and evidence are in place; remaining gaps stay labeled unknown.

Offering: Values — the Cursor skill that grills toward an outward north star. Exclusion for this map: not mapping the autonomy drive itself (or a product built around autonomy-as-primary). Autonomy stays important to retain, but centering it here would pull toward self-centered latent desire rather than looking for what others value.

Included: (1) Installable Cursor skill (global or local via npx skills / Values repo) that can be picked up and put down mid work-session; (2) a decision tool — not a planning tool — for deciding on values and making the product valuable to someone else; (3) reference/output files that carry decision memory (the whys) into later development planning and agent context.

Pain relievers (mostly hypothesis from lived use): (1) Mid-session grill shifts frame — more of one's own mind than pure coding-with-AI; calmer; exercises a part of the brain that atrophies under regular AI use. (2) Memory/reference files give endurance — work isn't wasted; an enduring record (like a finished vibe-coding artifact) that future decisions can stand on. (3) Decision tool steers toward choosing to be valuable to others, not only autonomous self — reduces pains of dead showcase / lack of interaction, eroded self-confidence and competence, diminished personal worth, and feeling less worthy of relationships with others.

evidence.claim: After weak showcase traction, members quit interacting with the group (go quiet)
evidence.source: owner observation of Discord showcase and group chat

decisions.reason: Scope Value Design to Discord friends who ship personal projects and want outward value, excluding vibecoders whose primary goal is self-amusement through absurd or novelty-first builds.

Autonomy (safe space to create with AI) is the unstated top priority; competence follows and is nearly equal; only after both are felt do they turn toward others' needs — family, close friends, Discord peers — and toward creating/finding value for that close group rather than isolating in AI work. Outward Discord value is the later move, not the entry wedge.

Autonomy elevated above prior framing: primary attraction of AI/vibe coding; developers are autonomy-starved in traditional work; maps to human need (Maslow-adjacent: autonomy, creativity, liberty, freedom). Competence follows; outward Discord value comes after both are felt.

Bounded segment, priority job sequence (autonomy → competence → value for close Discord others), pains, gains, alternatives, and labeled evidence are enough to leave the profile milestone; unknowns remain labeled not invented.

Map Values the Cursor skill only; autonomy is retained as important context but excluded from this value-map pass because autonomy-drive mapping pulls toward self-centered latent desire rather than outward value for others.

unknowns.question: How strongly autonomy-as-safe-space was evidenced before this priority turn (new framing vs prior accepted jobs)
